raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

LLaDA2 initializes its dLLM block size and mask ID from architecture defaults. Declared checkpoint metadata is not used to select these values. For block-routing checkpoints whose declared block size differs from the default, startup requires a matching manual override.

This PR reads the metadata for LLaDA2 while preserving the existing defaults when it is absent, following the scope discussed in #39499:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39499#issuecomment-6359947022

Related to #39499. Configuration overlap: #31586 and #44385.

## Modifications

- Read `block_size` from the effective model configuration, including JSON model overrides. Fall back to `32` only when the field is absent. Require a positive integer and reject a conflicting YAML value. YAML may supply the value when the checkpoint omits it.
- Resolve the selected tokenizer source through the existing tokenizer source resolver, preserving a separate tokenizer path. Resolve the declared `mask_token` against the selected serialized vocabulary and forward the configured revision. Preserve the existing mask ID when no mask is declared; reject a declared mask missing from the vocabulary, inconsistent IDs, and IDs outside the model vocabulary.
- Resolve the mask before validating the InDel token IDs. The metadata lookup does not execute a checkpoint's custom tokenizer Python code.
- Add regression coverage for metadata fallbacks, conflicts, versioned tokenizer-file selection, source resolution, and propagation through `ServerArgs` to page-size resolution. Document the supported behavior and limitations.

Other model families retain their existing behavior. Algorithm selection remains explicit because the inspected LLaDA2 checkpoints do not declare a default algorithm. Declared masks require a serialized fast tokenizer; slow-only tokenizers and custom code that changes token IDs are outside this lookup's scope.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested against upstream commit [`535aeae2`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/535aeae2a709077e3d17f5efc48350319ac13fc9) with this patch applied:

- 222 registered regression tests passed across six files, plus four committed-token/cache tests. All 226 selected tests passed without skips.
- Configuration checks passed for checkpoint defaults, YAML conflicts, separate tokenizer paths, and non-default block sizes/mask IDs.
- Versioned tokenizer and source-resolution regression tests passed. Source tests use real tokenizer files with mocked download/cache boundaries and do not access live cloud storage.
- Baseline and patched LLaDA2.2-mini BF16 inference produced identical `output_ids` for two prompts with decode CUDA Graph disabled and enabled. The scripts assert exact token-ID equality, and server logs confirm actual graph use in the enabled runs. Prefill CUDA Graph remained disabled.
- Pre-commit and documentation build/link checks passed.

The inference checks used `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.2-mini` at revision `e4f77d25ab5ca86f2223c6cdc6a72b887e20c8a5`, `JointThresholdInDel`, one GPU, one concurrent request, a 1,024-token context limit, temperature 0, and at most 32 new tokens. These are functional checks, not a full model-accuracy benchmark.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance improvement is claimed. This changes configuration resolution, not model kernels. No matched speed benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results: functional inference checks are reported above; full accuracy/speed benchmarks were not run.
- [x] Follow the repository code style.

@@ -33,6 +33,27 @@ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
 
 Depending on the algorithm selected, the configuration parameters vary.
 
+For LLaDA2, `block_size` defaults to the value in the checkpoint configuration,
+or `32` if the checkpoint does not declare it. You can set `block_size` in the
+YAML file when the checkpoint does not declare it. If both declare a value,
+they must match. The effective value must be a positive integer.
+
+LLaDA2 uses the tokenizer's declared `mask_token` and its ID in the serialized
+vocabulary selected by Transformers. Metadata lookup uses the same source
+resolution as the tokenizer loader and respects a separate `--tokenizer-path`.
+The vocabulary is `tokenizer.json` by default, or
+the compatible versioned file selected from `fast_tokenizer_files` in
+`tokenizer_config.json`. Standard fast-tokenizer loading resolves declarations in
+`tokenizer_config.json` and legacy `special_tokens_map.json`. If no mask token
+is declared, it falls back to the architecture default. A declared token that is missing
+from the tokenizer vocabulary or outside the model vocabulary causes an error.
+This metadata lookup does not execute custom tokenizer Python code.
+It requires a serialized fast tokenizer when a mask is declared, including
+when you use `--skip-tokenizer-init`. Custom tokenizer code that changes token
+IDs and slow-only tokenizer formats are not covered by this metadata lookup.
+Continue to select the decoding algorithm with `--dllm-algorithm`;
+the LLaDA2 checkpoints do not declare a default algorithm.
+
 LowConfidence Config:
 

@@ -182,3 +213,83 @@ def from_server_args(
             delete_token_id=delete_token_id,
             split_token_id=split_token_id,
         )
+
+
+def _require_llada2_block_size(block_size: Any) -> None:
+    if (
+        isinstance(block_size, bool)
+        or not isinstance(block_size, int)
+        or block_size <= 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"LLaDA2 block_size must be a positive integer, got {block_size!r}"
+        )
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
+def _checkpoint_mask_id(tokenizer_path: str, revision: str | None) -> int | None:
+    """Read declared mask metadata without initializing remote tokenizer code."""
+    from sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers.tokenizer import _resolve_tokenizer_name
+
+    tokenizer_path = _resolve_tokenizer_name(tokenizer_name=tokenizer_path, kwargs={})
+    has_mask = False
+    tokenizer_config = {}
+    for filename in ("tokenizer_config.json", "special_tokens_map.json"):
+        config_path = cached_file(
+            tokenizer_path,
+            filename,
+            revision=revision,
+            _raise_exceptions_for_missing_entries=False,
+        )
+        if config_path is not None:
+            with open(config_path) as f:
+                metadata = json.load(f)
+            if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
+                raise ValueError(f"{filename} at {tokenizer_path!r} must be a mapping")
+            if filename == "tokenizer_config.json":
+                tokenizer_config = metadata
+            has_mask |= metadata.get("mask_token") is not None
+    if not has_mask:
+        return None
+
+    # Let Transformers resolve legacy special-token maps and added-token metadata.
+    # Loading the concrete fast class never imports a checkpoint's custom Python.
+    from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
+
+    try:
+        tokenizer = PreTrainedTokenizerFast.from_pretrained(
+            tokenizer_path, revision=revision
+        )
+    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Invalid tokenizer mask_token metadata at {tokenizer_path!r}"
+        ) from exc
+    mask_token = tokenizer.mask_token
+    if mask_token is None:
+        return None
+    if not isinstance(mask_token, str) or not mask_token:
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid tokenizer mask_token: {mask_token!r}")
+
+    # A serialized fast tokenizer covers both added tokens and the base vocabulary.
+    # token_to_id returns None for a missing token instead of the unknown-token ID.
+    from tokenizers import Tokenizer
+    from transformers.tokenization_utils_base import get_fast_tokenizer_file
+
+    tokenizer_filename = "tokenizer.json"
+    if "fast_tokenizer_files" in tokenizer_config:
+        tokenizer_filename = get_fast_tokenizer_file(
+            tokenizer_config["fast_tokenizer_files"]
+        )
+    tokenizer_file = cached_file(tokenizer_path, tokenizer_filename, revision=revision)
+    token_id = Tokenizer.from_file(tokenizer_file).token_to_id(mask_token)
+    if token_id is None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Tokenizer mask_token {mask_token!r} is absent from its vocabulary "
+            f"at {tokenizer_path!r}"
+        )
+    if tokenizer.mask_token_id != token_id:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Conflicting mask IDs at {tokenizer_path!r}: tokenizer metadata "
+            f"resolves {tokenizer.mask_token_id}, {tokenizer_filename} declares {token_id}"
+        )
+    return token_id
